issues.detail: The Hebrew 'אֵל יִדְּפֶנּוּ לֹא אִישׁ' means 'God will rebuke him, not a man' (or 'God will pursue him, not a man'), i.e., it is God, not a man, who will drive him away. The Chinese renders it as '人不能勝過他，連神也不能' ('man cannot overcome him, even God cannot'), which reverses the meaning: the Hebrew says God (not man) will do the action, while the Chinese says neither man nor God can overcome him. This changes the subject and negates the divine action.
